chapter: Becoming a musician: ukulele, clarinet and the Boozaire Kings
title: Chords, uncles' drums and Paul Barbarin's clarinet
summary: Learning three chords from Herman Henderson, getting by on the drums his uncles showed him, and trying Uncle Paul's clarinet.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: The changes. And three chords, C-F-G. But in the meantime, I had been around my uncle Paul between his visits from Chicago, and my uncle Louis and them, and they all got this drum set up, and they'd play... All of them played the drums. So I could get by on the drums, too. They showed me how to hold the sticks properly and they let me play. And my aunt had bought a victrola, and they'd go borrow the victrola in (?), and they'd play against the victrola. And they'd let me play. Then I thought about all them drums you have to carry.

So my Uncle Paul has got a clarinet. He's foolin' around with the clarinet. Can't play it. He's foolin' around, but he's learning to... I found out later that he was learning so he could count, count notation to write, because he wanted to write. So he figured he'd play a little melody and he'd be able to. So he let me blow the clarinet. A lift-off(?) point. He told me, 'Go take some lessons.'
